question: Healthy eyes in Eritrea and meerkats that find their way home

stories.headline: Eritrea beats an eye sickness
stories.deck: A simple plan helped stop trachoma from being a big health problem.
body: Trachoma is an eye sickness caused by tiny germs called bacteria. If people catch it again and again, it can make them blind.
On November 16, the World Health Organization said Eritrea, in East Africa, has beaten trachoma as a public health problem. It is the 34th country to do this.
Eritrea used a plan called SAFE: surgery, antibiotic medicines, clean faces, and a better environment, like clean water and toilets.
evidence: Trachoma is a sickness of the eyes. It is caused by tiny germs called bacteria.
On November 16, the World Health Organization, called WHO, said Eritrea has beaten trachoma as a public health problem. It is the 34th country in the world to do this.
It used a plan called SAFE. S is for surgery. A is for antibiotics, medicines that fight bacteria. F is for clean faces. E is for a better environment, like clean water and toilets.
stories.why: Simple things, like clean water and medicine, can protect people's eyes.

stories.headline: Meerkats find the way home
stories.deck: Alone and far from their group, most meerkats walked straight back.
body: Scientists in the Kalahari Desert, in southern Africa, put GPS collars on meerkats. Then they took one meerkat at a time 1.5 kilometres away and let it go.
Each meerkat stood up on its back legs to look around. Then it walked in a straight line. It stopped now and then to look again or to sniff for smells it knew.
In 20 tries, 18 meerkats went straight back. The other two may have been too stressed to move.
evidence: Meerkats are small animals that live in groups in the Kalahari Desert, in southern Africa.
Each meerkat stood up on its back legs to look around. Then it walked in a straight line, stopping now and then to look again or to sniff for smells it knew.
18 of the 20 meerkats went straight back to their group or to the spot where they were caught. The other two may have been too stressed to move.
stories.why: Meerkats live in groups, but each one seems to know the way by itself.
